hyps.why: With edge 3 absent, edge 4 is part of the only remaining input-to-output paths, so removing it cuts connectivity and collapses accuracy (rows 55, 57, 59).
If edge 5 is none, removing edge 4 severs the 1->3 path and leaves little connectivity, giving huge drops (rows 57, 59).
Replacing none with skip adds a new direct input-to-output path, whereas replacing a learned conv with skip usually helps little or hurts (rows 24, 25 vs 26, 28, 30).
Adding a 3x3 conv where the direct edge was absent adds a path and capacity, giving larger gains than swapping one existing op for another (rows 74, 77, 79).
When edge 5 is none the cell depends on edge 3 and the 1->3 path, so upgrading edge 3 matters much more (row 79: +78).
With edge 5 disabled, edge 3 is a critical route to the output, so a working op there gives a large gain (row 25: +74).
When edge 4 is none, fewer paths reach the output, so strengthening the direct edge 3 helps more (rows 78, 79).
A skip on edge 3 restores connectivity when edge 4 is missing, with the biggest gains where other paths are dead (row 25).
Deleting a trained 3x3 conv removes real capacity and sometimes the key path, so it is consistently harmful (rows 52, 55, 57, 60).
Replacing none with skip adds a new connection into the output node, which tends to help more than replacing an existing conv with skip (row 95 vs 91, 92).
